avalancheProblems.comment:
The southerly foehn wind will transport the new snow. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches easily. Avalanches can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers. Mostly they are medium-sized. Additionally in isolated cases avalanches can also be released in the old snowpack and reach large size. This applies especially on north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m.
Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Snow depths are well above average. Over a wide area, there is twice to three times as much snow as is usual for the time of year. Weak layers prone to triggering are still found primarily in the sometimes thick new and wind-drifted snow layers of recent days. These are stabilizing rapidly.
Above approximately 2600 m, on north- and east-facing slopes, coarse-grained old snow is in some places still found at the snow base. This near-ground old snow has now been overlain by layers so thick that fractures in near-ground layers of the snowpack are not very likely.

Above approximately 2600 m, on north- and east-facing slopes, coarse-grained old snow is in some places still found at the snow base. This near-ground old snow has now been overlain by layers so thick that fractures in near-ground layers of the snowpack are not very likely.

tendency.comment:
Wet-snow avalanches

Gliding avalanches can be released at any time of day or night. They can reach large size. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided.

Dry avalanches

The danger of dry avalanches will gradually decrease. However, persons can release avalanches as before. Careful route selection is required.

avalancheProblems.comment:
As a consequence of a moderate to strong southerly wind, avalanche prone wind slabs will form over a wide area. Additionally in some places avalanches can also be released in the old snowpack and reach medium size. This applies especially on north and east facing slopes. Avalanches can be released, even by a single winter sport participant.
Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.

CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "considerable" (3-) in west to northeast to southeast facing aspects above 2200m.

snowpackStructure.comment: The snow depths are below average for the time of year and are scarcely sufficient for snow sports in open terrain. Especially on shady slopes with a smooth ground surface above approximately 2400 m, there is a cohesive layer of coarse-grained, weak old snow at the snow base. These weak layers are overlain by mostly thin layers of new and wind-drifted snow from the last week and are prone to triggering.

tendency.comment: The danger of dry avalanches will increase slightly. Even single winter sport participants can release avalanches, including in deeper layers. Backcountry touring and other off-piste activities call for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.

avalancheProblems.comment:
As a consequence of a moderate to strong southerly wind, avalanche prone wind slabs will form over a wide area. Additionally in some places avalanches can also be released in the old snowpack and reach medium size. This applies especially on north and east facing slopes. Avalanches can be released, even by a single winter sport participant.
Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.

CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "considerable" (3-) in west to northeast to southeast facing aspects above 2200m.
